correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the defining Lie and 3-Lie Reynolds identities and performs exact symbolic elimination. The resulting eleven equations admit a complete case split on the second column of the matrix, yielding exactly X1 or X2. Direct reduction verifies the converse on both components. Irreducibility and dimensions follow from the two irreducible quadratic equations, and the component intersection follows by adding their ideals. The packaged verifier independently reconstructs the defects and all critical polynomial computations.

value.rationale: Example 4.4 is the paper's explicit low-dimensional realization of its Lie-to-3-Lie Reynolds construction. Completing its parameter space is mathematically substantive because the omitted sets are positive-dimensional divisors, not isolated corner cases. The correction replaces two denominator-dependent formulas by a denominator-free exact variety, identifies two irreducible five-dimensional components and their intersection, and supplies concrete missing operators usable as regression examples for future classifications.
